purpose: Audit/refactor note: hazard class and consequence class should be queryable across engineering records without becoming an after-the-fact moral label.
findings: Structural, process-safety, nuclear, and impoundment records all need a distinction between physical failure mode and consequence exposure.

Tailings records especially require denominator/disclosure surfaces: not only what failed, but how many facilities, where, under whose control, with what hazard classification, and with what public accountability.
The cube should avoid using fatalities or environmental damage as the sole risk proxy; exposure, warning time, material/runout behavior, emergency planning, and governance matter separately.

future_refactors.action: Add optional hazard_classification_overlay with exposure, warning-time, material/runout, and emergency-planning fields.
Add explicit factor-axis edges after current overlay stabilizes.
Require each engineering pattern to name at least one control where consequence exposure was high but hazard was intercepted or mitigated.
